canonical_data: A local git repository of plain files holding each agent's memory, inbox and outbox, with a derived semantic recall index over the markdown memory
current_repo_note: Covers the open-source desktop application in the repository, which GitHub now serves under HarnessMD/munder-difflin and redirects from the chaitanyagiri name this record keeps. The README advertises a paid Pro tier, including a meeting-transcription feature, whose code was not found in the source tree, so those features and their terms are not reviewed here. The bundled pixel-art tilesets are licensed separately from the MIT source.
strengths: Each agent is the real vendor CLI in its own pseudo-terminal rather than a re-implementation, so the harness adds coordination without replacing what the CLI does
A documented circuit-breaker policy escalates from steering to constraining to stopping, with the hard stop off by default, because the wrapped CLI exposes no dollar ceiling of its own
Coordination state is plain files in a local git repository with a single committer, so a person can read, edit, and diff what the agents said to each other
weaknesses: The project is pre-release at version 0.5.3 and was created in May 2026, so interfaces and storage layouts are still changing
Human approvals are left to each wrapped CLI's own session, because the hive has no separate approval queue, so oversight differs by provider
A paid Pro tier is advertised in the README while the code for its features is absent from the repository, which leaves part of the product outside the reviewed licence
why_it_matters: A fast-growing open-source take on running a team of the coding CLIs people already pay for, with real message routing, shared memory, and runaway-cost guardrails rather than a dashboard over independent sessions.
